name: T.M.
occupation: Student (App State, NC), recreation management + park ranger experience
presenting: Unresolved childhood trauma affecting self-esteem, confidence, assertiveness, and trust. Anxiety-driven hypervigilance. Difficulty letting go and feeling comfortable in own skin.
presenting_quote: I have some issues with letting go of past traumatic experiences and the feelings surrounding them from when I was a young kid. I've tried traditional psychotherapy, which has helped a ton, but I am still looking to resolve complicated feelings around self-esteem, confidence, assertiveness, and generally to feel comfortable in my own skin. I have issues letting go and trusting people that are close to me. It still feels like my anxiety still runs the show sometimes, and I want to become more open and less hypervigilant.
prior_therapy: Traditional psychotherapy (client reports significant progress but unresolved feelings remain)
history: 22-year-old student at Appalachian State University, North Carolina. Living with grandfather. Support system: few childhood friends + sister. Childhood abuse from family members including mother. Feelings: abandoned, alone, betrayed, angry, ashamed. Difficulty forming close relationships due to trust issues and fear of vulnerability. Prior psychotherapy helped significantly. Triggers: men yelling (causes fear and anxiety), past trauma discussions. Wants: emotional stability, assertiveness, awareness of past without current anxiety. Forgiveness not fully achieved on past events. CSP pro bono client via HMI. Requested male therapist.
contraindications: Childhood abuse (family members, mother) - ongoing emotional impact
Trigger: men yelling - causes fear/anxiety response
Trigger: past trauma discussions - exacerbates symptoms
Trigger: feeling disrespected/demeaned/undermined - activates anger + shame cycle
Abandonment/betrayal pattern - affects trust in close relationships
Fear of vulnerability - guard stays up, especially in group settings
Self-labeling pattern - binds behavior to identity (calls self 'asshole' when judgmental)
Recurring nightmares - fighting, being attacked, revenge, lost friendship

triggering_incident.situation: Customer at parks job arrived without knowing rules/costs, became angry when informed, glared with dismissive attitude, expected discount Tristan could not provide
triggering_incident.client_internal: Perceived disrespect, internally judged customer as 'bad person who doesn't care about other people'. Remained calm outwardly but judgment troubled him. Triggered broader feeling of 'being a bad person'.
triggering_incident.clinical_significance: Pre-existing negative self-image activated by external event. Cycle: trigger (disrespect) > anger > guilt about anger > self-labeling > shame.

soap.objective: 69% Emotional suggestibility confirmed in delivery responsiveness. Session adapted from scripted protocol to address client-presented triggering incident and vulnerability patterns. Induction: breathing + spoken affirmations ('I am great', 'I am a wonderful person', 'Everybody genuinely likes me', 'I am being loved') + hand on chest + eyes-open visual anchoring (own face expressing pride/bravery) + Deep Sleep keyword. Deepened: 5-0 countdown + 10-0 staircase + full body scan (crown to toes, negative experiences reframed as empathy training). Hypnodrama Tribe Circle: 11 soul tribe members in circle, each radiating specific quality (bravery, motherly care, self-esteem, belonging). Members invited one by one, all 11 integrated into body sequentially, sealed with golden light protective aura. Anchor installed: thumb + forefinger (RIGHT hand) = integrated/protected/self-assured state, reinforced 2x. Post-trance: client reported feeling 'more steady', described sensation as 'almost like an armor or a shield'. Engaged authentically with identity-vs-behavior reframe, projection/shadow work, Snake and Saint parable.
soap.assessment: First formal trance session. Client demonstrates meaningful S1-to-S2 progress: spontaneous observer-stance toward negative thoughts. Core behavioral loop identified: perceived disrespect > defensive anger > guilt about anger > self-labeling as bad person > shame. Self-labeling pattern (behavior = identity) is damaging self-esteem and must be interrupted. Fear of vulnerability in groups directly connected to betrayal/abandonment wounds. Hypnodrama tribe circle created corrective group experience in trance -- client experienced being surrounded by supportive figures without threat. Rescuer-helper identity reframe provides new behavioral framework (victim > healer arc). Anchor (thumb + forefinger, RIGHT hand) reported as effective ('armor/shield'). Prognosis: good. Client responsive to trance, engages authentically, shows between-session progress. NOTE: SMART baselines not yet collected (deferred -- collect at S2b start). Formal 3-wound identification (Lisa method) not completed -- wound material addressed organically through presenting incident.

Reversal suggestion + compound anchor. 3. COLLECT SMART BASELINES at S2b start (deferred from S1 and S2a). 4. Circle of Trust (graduated trust ring visualization) for S3. 5.
